summary.oneLiner: Mangalam Global Enterprise Limited is a Gujarat-based agri-processing and edible/non-edible oil manufacturer and trader that operates four plants and is extending downstream into a branded B2C wellness and nutraceutical business, Neat Everyday.
summary.business: The Company is mainly engaged in the manufacturing, trading and import of edible and non-edible oils and agricultural products - soya oil, soya meal and de-oiled cake, mustard oil, mustard meal and de-oiled cake, refined soyabean and refined vegetable oil, pungent mustard oil, refined castor oil First Special Grade (FSG), castor de-oiled cake and high protein castor de-oiled cake, cotton bales, cotton cake cattle feed and cotton wash oil - together with the processing of wheat and rice. It also trades agricultural products such as wheat and rice in both domestic and export markets. During the year it moved into the Business-to-Consumer segment with its wellness and personal-care brand Neat Everyday, selling 100% vegetarian nutraceuticals, supplements and cold-pressed oils through an omnichannel model.

Edible & non-edible oils and meals: Refined Castor Oil First Special Grade (FSG)
B2C wellness & personal care (Neat Every: Evening Primrose Oil Soft Vegan Capsules

currentContext.strengths: Diversified multi-crop processing base - castor, cotton, wheat and rice, and soya/mustard oils and meals - run across four plants in Gujarat, so the Company is not tied to a single crop cycle|Presence across both manufacturing and domestic/export trading of agricultural products, giving multiple routes to market for the same crop complex|Raw-material adjacency between the core oil-processing business and the new Neat Everyday cold-pressed oil and nutraceutical range (castor oil, mustard oil), letting the B2C brand build on existing processing capability|Move into a higher-margin branded B2C portfolio: management states each incremental Neat Everyday sale is expected to be earnings accretive, supported by the higher margins associated with these products|Omnichannel retail model for Neat Everyday combining own stores (five simultaneously inaugurated in Ahmedabad, in addition to existing stores) with wider India accessibility|Listed history and upgrade in listing status - originally listed on the NSE Emerge SME platform in November 2019, shares now listed on both NSE and BSE
currentContext.strategies: Decisive shift into the Business-to-Consumer (B2C) segment through the wellness brand Neat Everyday, described as a bold and strategic leap aimed at the demand for clean, natural and science-backed health products.|Deepen presence in the wellness and nutraceutical sector by widening the Neat Everyday portfolio - now a comprehensive range of 100% vegetarian nutraceutical and personal-care products formulated from natural ingredients and supported by scientific validation.|Build an organised-retail footprint: expand to 100 new Neat Everyday stores/outlets by March 2028, after launching the brand with the simultaneous inauguration of five retail stores across Ahmedabad, Gujarat in addition to existing stores.|Run an omnichannel business model for Neat Everyday designed to enhance customer accessibility and engagement across India, positioning the brand around purity, hygiene, affordability and customer trust.|Stay diversified across the agri-commodity complex - manufacturing, trading and import of edible and non-edible oils, castor, cotton, soya and mustard products, and wheat and rice processing - combined with domestic and export trading of agricultural products.|Extend the group structure into new trading and organic/plant-based verticals through subsidiaries: MGEL Multicomm Private Limited (incorporated January 3, 2025) for multi-commodity trading and distribution, and Mangalam Vanasya Organic Private Limited (incorporated January 22, 2026) for wholesale, trading, distribution, import, export, processing and formulation of agricultural raw materials and plant-based materials, alongside the Singapore wholly owned subsidiary Mangalam Global (Singapore) Pte Ltd for wholesale trade.
currentContext.expansion: Expansion in this annual report is retail- and brand-led rather than plant-led. The Company launched its wellness and personal-care brand Neat Everyday through the simultaneous inauguration of five retail stores across Ahmedabad, Gujarat, in addition to existing stores, and during the year announced a strategic expansion plan to establish 100 new Neat Everyday stores/outlets by March 2028 to strengthen its retail footprint and enhance customer accessibility across key markets, aiming to build its presence in the organised retail segment. The Neat Everyday product portfolio was itself further expanded during the year to a comprehensive range of 100% vegetarian nutraceutical and personal-care products, including premium cold-pressed oils, soft capsules and gummies. On the manufacturing side the Directors' Report states only that the Company presently operates four plants (Unit Bavla, Sanand, Gujarat for wheat and rice processing; Unit Kapadvanj, Kheda, Gujarat for castor oil; Unit Kapadvanj, Kheda, Gujarat for cotton; the fourth was cut from the routed excerpt) with no new line, debottlenecking or commissioning programme described. Group footprint was extended through subsidiaries rather than greenfield capacity: MGEL Multicomm Private Limited (India, incorporated January 3, 2025) for multi-commodity trading and distribution and Mangalam Vanasya Organic Private Limited (India, incorporated January 22, 2026) for agricultural raw materials and plant-based materials, alongside the wholly owned Mangalam Global (Singapore) Pte Ltd. The accounts disclose that the estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account was NIL at both 31 March 2026 and 31 March 2025, so no contracted capital expenditure was outstanding at year end.
currentContext.mdna: Management states the NEAT EVERYDAY product range has been receiving strong market acceptance and positive consumer response, and that each incremental sale is expected to be earnings accretive on the higher margins associated with these products - i.e. mix shift towards branded B2C is the stated margin lever.|MD&A frames the India nutraceuticals opportunity as structural: a proactive, preventive approach to well-being post-pandemic, rising prevalence of lifestyle diseases, urbanisation and sedentary lifestyles, a burgeoning middle class with rising disposable incomes, and consumer preference for natural, plant-based and Ayurveda-inspired clean-label products - reinforced by clear FSSAI regulation building consumer trust (third-party market data cited).|Distribution narrative for nutraceuticals: supermarkets and hypermarkets dominate with a health aisle concept and premium shelf space, while online channels are the fast-growing route because digital storefronts carry certifications, ingredient sourcing, third-party lab results and user reviews - supporting the omnichannel approach.|Castor oil demand outlook: growing demand for bio-based chemicals, pharmaceutical excipients and specialty lubricants makes castor oil a strategic raw material; sustainability trends favour it as a renewable, biodegradable substitute for petroleum-derived oils; and export-based manufacturing from Asia is expanding global trade flows as multinational buyers diversify sourcing.|Castor oil demand also underpinned by animal feed - compound cattle feed adoption by milk producers and castor's ricinoleic acid content - and by the growth of green cosmetics, where castor is cited as one of the best natural, non-toxic green raw materials.|Stated castor-oil headwinds: wavering raw-material prices, since castor bean prices rise rapidly under insufficient irrigation and water scarcity, squeezing downstream production, demand and profit margins; and lipid oxidation limiting shelf life, which pushes some producers towards alternatives.|Cotton outlook: market growing at a modest CAGR with Asia-Pacific holding the largest share on China's spinning industry and India's role as largest producer and leading exporter, with biotech seed adoption and regenerative-agriculture premiums as tailwinds against water scarcity, rising input costs and pest resistance.|India rice outlook: steady growth on a large population base, MSP-driven procurement, agricultural modernisation, expanding organised retail and e-commerce, premiumisation with rising incomes, and India's strengthening position in global rice trade - in a fragmented competitive landscape of regional processors and millers where players compete on brand differentiation, quality certifications and distribution reach.|Wheat outlook: staple demand for more than 2.5 billion people, public-health fortification programmes and biofuel-mandate-driven industrial demand, with Asia-Pacific anchoring consumption on resilient state support in China and India and record Indian production and sowing area.|Mustard and soyabean oil outlook: mustard oil demand supported by its MUFA and omega-3 profile and health positioning plus growing personal-care and cosmetics use; soybean oil demand driven by food processors and food-service users, the biodiesel and renewable-fuel industry, and rising consumer preference for non-GMO and organic soy products.

risks.risk: Castor raw-material price volatility tied to water availability
risks.note: The MD&A castor-oil section states that castor oil output is influenced by warmth, sunlight, precipitation, soil, latitude and altitude, that farmers are finding it tough to continue farming due to a lack of water, and that owing to insufficient irrigation the price of castor beans rises rapidly - with the explicit consequence that fluctuating prices 'have an impact on downstream production and demand for castor oil, lowering profit margins'. Castor oil (refined FSG, de-oiled cake, high-protein DOC) is one of the Company's core manufactured lines and is run out of a dedicated plant at Kapadvanj, Kheda.

risks.risk: Product-quality / shelf-life exposure in castor oil (lipid oxidation)
risks.note: The MD&A notes that castor oil's lipid structure contains double bonds that undergo lipid oxidation, generating peroxides and altering the chemical composition of the oil, and that this makes it difficult for producers to employ castor oil and pushes them to seek alternatives, limiting market development - a substitution and quality-control risk for a castor-led product portfolio.

risks.risk: Cotton value-chain headwinds: water scarcity, input costs and pest resistance
risks.note: The MD&A cotton section states that water scarcity, rising input costs and pest resistance are tempering the expansion of the cotton market even as Asia-Pacific demand, biotech uptake and sustainability premiums drive growth. The Company runs a dedicated cotton unit at Kapadvanj, Kheda producing cotton bales, cotton cake cattle feed and cotton wash oil.

risks.risk: Fragmented, low-differentiation competition in the Indian agri-commodity and rice market
risks.note: The MD&A describes the India rice market as a fragmented competitive landscape with numerous regional processors, traditional millers and organised players competing across value-added and commodity segments, where participants must compete on brand differentiation, quality certifications and distribution network expansion - the same battleground the Company's wheat and rice processing and trading business operates in.

risks.risk: Macro and geopolitical downside to Indian demand and input costs
risks.note: The MD&A cites the World Bank's projection of India growth at 6.6% in FY27, with higher energy prices caused by the Middle East conflict and supply-chain disruptions weighing on economic activity, and flags significant downside risks stemming from the conflict, partially insulated by strong macroeconomic fundamentals, foreign reserves, low inflation and trade diversification. As a manufacturer, importer and exporter of agricultural commodities, the Company is exposed to both energy costs and trade-flow disruption.

risks.risk: Commodity-crop dependence on monsoon, agro-climatic conditions and government policy
risks.note: Across the routed MD&A sections, output and pricing for the crops the Company processes and trades - castor, cotton, rice and wheat - are described as functions of irrigation, monsoon conditions, agro-climatic factors, minimum support price mechanisms and government procurement and cultivation initiatives, so earnings depend on variables outside management control.
